classification.difficultyReason: Same structure as the reference: a population SD by calculator, then the effect of a constant increase, then a percentage increase, then a comparison.

content.prompt:
A landscaping business has five workers. Their weekly wages are:
$\$420,\ \$520,\ \$580,\ \$640,\ \$840$

children.label: a
children.prompt: Calculate the population standard deviation for this set of data, rounded to the nearest dollar.

answer.worked:
Enter the five wages in the calculator's 1-variable statistics mode and select population standard deviation $\sigma_x$.
$$\begin{aligned}\sigma_x &\approx \$140.2854\\&\approx \$140\quad\text{(nearest dollar)}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Each worker receives a $\$30$ pay increase. Explain the effect that this increase will have on the standard deviation.

answer.short: Unchanged; the spread of the wages is unchanged.
answer.worked: Every wage and the mean increase by $\$30$, so each wage's distance from the mean stays the same. The standard deviation is unchanged.

children.label: c
children.prompt: Instead of the $\$30$ increase, every worker receives a 5% pay rise. Calculate the new population standard deviation to the nearest dollar.

answer.worked:
New wages: $\$441,\ \$546,\ \$609,\ \$672,\ \$882$. Enter these in 1-variable statistics mode and select $\sigma_x$.
$$\begin{aligned}\sigma_x &\approx \$147.2997\\&\approx \$147\quad\text{(nearest dollar)}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: d
children.prompt: Which pay rise gives the smaller standard deviation: $\$30$ each or 5% each?

answer.worked: The $\$30$ pay increase leaves the standard deviation at approximately $\$140$. The 5% pay rise increases it to approximately $\$147$, so $\$30$ each gives the smaller standard deviation.
